I like everybody. (except for people that come into the store and treat their children badly.) And I especially like homeless people. On one level I blame their homelessness on a system that ignores problems of mental health, poverty, and young poor families whose caretakers have mental health issues. (The U.S.) I've seen how easy it is for a huge segment of my city to go from "scraping by" to "pack your tee-shirts and some diapers into a trash bag and steal some shopping carts because everybody's homeless."

On another level I feel like everyone would be a lot happier if we decided to go homeless as a community. Obviously resources are important, but I'm not sure that being used to the comforts that a sealed capsule provides make for the most rugged and useful bunch of people, physically or mentally.

But I'm no expert. I work at a gas station that had the gas pumps pulled out of it.

Anyway, meet a lot of homeless. There is one I am thinking of in particular.

Her name is Tanya. She could be thirty, hard to tell, and she comes in to make herself coffee in her thermos with our hot water and creamers. She always very politely asks if she can use a coupe of creamers and sugars.

One morning I was refreshing the coffee and Tanya came in. She waited for my manager to finish her transaction before making her request, then proceed back to the coffee bar where I was working. I then asked her about her morning. It was a short, simple conversation, and I didn't think anything about it.

Ten minutes later I went on break and I see Tanya walking towards me. She hands me ten dollars. I try to argue ("I get paid every day") but after three times trying to refuse without her backing off i meagerly accepted and thanked her. She smiled and walked off without explanation.

-

I don't know the moral of the story or even understand it, but may I suggest that you make a point of having simple and pleasant conversations with homeless people, especially regulars. There is a chance it will make them happy.
